answer: I would like to talk about the most well-travelled person in my family. A person who has travelled extensively is an uncle of mine, my mother's elder brother, who spent much of his career working abroad as an engineer. He has lived on several continents and visited dozens of countries, from the Gulf to Malaysia, Germany and Canada, and his stories are genuinely [[captivating]]. He has recently moved back to Bangladesh and lives in Dhaka, so I see him whenever I visit my elder sister there. What I find most interesting is not the places themselves, but how travel has shaped his outlook; he is remarkably [[tolerant]] and open to different ways of life. He often says that seeing how others live cured him of taking anything for granted. He also learned to be patient and adaptable, because nothing abroad ever went quite according to plan, from missed trains to misunderstood menus. Listening to him is almost like receiving [[an informal education]] in geography and culture. I think people who travel widely tend to develop a certain wisdom that is hard to gain any other way. As for how I feel about his experiences, I am a little envious, to be honest, and his stories have made me determined to explore more of the world myself, starting, I hope, with studying abroad. Whenever I hear them, I feel a pang of [[wanderlust]] and a renewed appreciation for how [[vast]] and varied the world really is.

followUps.q: Would you like to travel as much as he has?
followUps.answer: I would love to, although perhaps not for work. I would rather travel slowly, spending weeks in one place to properly [[soak up]] the culture, instead of rushing from city to city.

followUps.q: Which country would you most like to visit?
followUps.answer: Probably Canada or the UK, partly because many of my students go there and I would like to see what their lives are like. I am also fascinated by Japan's mix of tradition and technology.

note: Added who he is (mother's brother, engineer, now in Dhaka), where he has been and what he learned, and linked it to my study-abroad plans; mark moved to 'an informal education', added 'wanderlust'.
